Per bun-types@1.3.14:

The `bun-types` package defines two distinct SQL APIs: a synchronous SQLite API via `bun:sqlite` and an asynchronous general SQL client (`SQL` class) for Postgres/MySQL. The SQLite `Database` class provides `run(sql, bindings)` (returns `Changes`) and `query(sql)`/`prepare(sql)` (returns a `Statement`). Parameterized queries use positional placeholders (`?`) with array bindings or named parameters (`$name`, `:name`, `@name`) with object bindings. The async `SQL` class uses tagged template literals (e.g., `sql\`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}\``) returning a `SQL.Query<T>` (a Promise), and supports helper functions like `sql(obj)` for dynamic column/value insertion.

Per bun-types@1.3.14:

The `SQL` class has three constructor overloads accepting `(connectionString: string | URL)`, `(connectionString, options)`, or `(options?)`. It implements `AsyncDisposable` and provides prototype methods including the callable template literal/string signatures returning `SQL.Query<T>`, helper functions for object/serializable insertion returning `SQL.Helper<T>`, transaction methods (`transaction`, `beginDistributed`/`distributed`, `commitDistributed`, `rollbackDistributed`), utility methods (`unsafe`, `file`), and disposal via `[Symbol.asyncDispose]()`. The `SQL.Query<T>` interface extends `Promise<T>` with properties `active` and `cancelled`, and methods `cancel()`, `simple()`, `execute()`, `raw()`, and `values()`.

Per bun-types@1.3.14:

Bun.file is not a class with a constructor; it is a function that returns a `BunFile` object. It has three overloads: accepting a `string | URL` path, an `ArrayBufferLike | Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` byte buffer path, or a numeric file descriptor, all optionally taking `BlobPropertyBag` options. The returned `BunFile` implements the `Blob` interface, providing methods like `text()`, `arrayBuffer()`, `bytes()`, `json()`, `formData()`, `stream()`, and `image()` for reading file contents lazily.

Source excerpt:
> /**
>    * [`Blob`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Blob) powered by the fastest system calls available for operating on files.
>    *
>    * This Blob is lazy. That means it won't do any work until you read from it.
>    *
>    * - `size` will not be valid until the contents of the file are read at least once.
>    * - `type` is auto-set based on the file extension when possible
>    *
>    * @example
>    * ```js
>    * const file = Bun.file("./hello.json");
>    * console.log(file.type); // "application/json"
>    * console.log(await file.json()); // { hello: "world" }
>    * ```
>    *
>    * @example
>    * ```js
>    * await Bun.write(
>    *   Bun.file("./hello.txt"),
>    *   "Hello, world!"
>    * );
>    * ```
>    * @param path The path to the file (lazily loaded) if the path starts with `s3://` it will behave like {@link S3File}
>    */
>   function file(path: string | URL, options?: BlobPropertyBag): BunFile;

`sql.unsafe()` is a method on the Bun SQL client that allows executing raw SQL strings without parameterization, returning an `SQL.Query<T>`. It accepts a SQL string and optional values array. Additionally, the `SQL.Query` interface provides a `.raw()` method that returns the raw query result.

>      * Please note that this can lead to SQL injection if you're not careful.
>      * You can also nest sql.unsafe within a safe sql expression. This is useful if only part of your fraction has unsafe elements.
>      * @example
>      * const result = await sql.unsafe(`select ${danger} from users where id = ${dragons}`)
>      */
>     unsafe<T = any>(string: string, values?: any[]): SQL.Query<T>;

The `SQL` class is defined in the `Bun` namespace with constructors accepting a connection string (`string | URL`) or `SQL.Options`. The `sql` tagged template literal is exposed via the callable signature on the `SQL` interface: `<T = any>(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]): SQL.Query<T>`. There is no `Bun.sql` global function shown; instead, you instantiate `new Bun.SQL()` and use its instance as a tagged template. For password hashing with argon2id, the provided content does not contain any types or definitions for `password.hash` or argon2id.

>      * @example
>      * ```ts
>      * const sql = new SQL("postgres://localhost:5432/mydb");

Per zod@4.4.3:

Use `z.object()` to define an object schema with primitive fields like `z.string()` and `z.number()`. Chain `.optional()` and `.nullable()` on individual fields or the whole schema to allow undefined/null values. Extract the output type using `z.infer<typeof schema>` and the input type using `z.input<typeof schema>`, which diverge when transforms are applied.

Source excerpt:
> In some cases, the input & output types of a schema can diverge. For instance, the `.transform()` API can convert the input from one type to another. In these cases, you can extract the input and output types independently:
> 
> ```ts
> const mySchema = z.string().transform((val) => val.length);
> 
> type MySchemaIn = z.input<typeof mySchema>;
> // => string
> 
> type MySchemaOut = z.output<typeof mySchema>; // equivalent to z.infer<typeof mySchema>
> // number
> ```

For POST body validation, use `zValidator('json', schema)` and access validated data via `c.req.valid('json')`. For GET query params, pass `'query'` as the target: `zValidator('query', schema)`. Per zod@4.4.3:

In Zod v4, `safeParse` returns `ZodSafeParseResult<core.output<T>>` synchronously, while `safeParseAsync` returns `Promise<ZodSafeParseResult<core.output<T>>>`. Both are generic functions accepting a schema (`T extends core.$ZodType`), an unknown value, and an optional parse context. The result is a discriminated union with a `success` boolean flag: on failure (`success: false`), the object contains an `error` property of type `ZodError<T>`; on success, it contains a `data` property with the parsed output.

zValidator is middleware that parses and validates the request body (e.g., via `c.req.json()`) against a Zod schema, storing the result so you can retrieve it later with `c.req.valid('json')`. The resize method signature is `resize([width], [height], [options])`. Width and height are optional number parameters that can also be set via `options.width` and `options.height`. The fit options are: 'cover' (default, crops to fill), 'contain' (letterboxes to fit), 'fill' (stretches ignoring aspect ratio), 'inside' (scales down to fit within dimensions), and 'outside' (scales up to exceed dimensions). The `withoutEnlargement` option prevents scaling up if either dimension is already smaller than the target. To constrain only the longest edge, use the `inside` fit with a square dimension (equal width and height), which scales the image to be as large as possible while fitting within both dimensions, effectively constraining the longest edge.

> 
> -   `cover`: (default) Preserving aspect ratio, attempt to ensure the image covers both provided dimensions by cropping/clipping to fit.
> -   `contain`: Preserving aspect ratio, contain within both provided dimensions using "letterboxing" where necessary.
> -   `fill`: Ignore the aspect ratio of the input and stretch to both provided dimensions.

For screenshots, use await expect(await mount('Story/Id')).toHaveScreenshot('file.png') on the mount locator. For network mocking, use page.route() before calling mount(), since mounting navigates to the page.

To set up shadcn with Tailwind v4, use the CLI to initialize a new project (which defaults to Tailwind v4 and React 19), or follow the upgrade guide for existing projects: (1) run the Tailwind v4 upgrade guide and `@tailwindcss/upgrade@next` codemod; (2) migrate CSS variables by moving `:root`/`.dark` out of `@layer base`, wrapping color values in `hsl()`, using `@theme inline`, and removing `hsl()` wrappers from `@theme`; (3) update chart colors to use `var()` directly; (4) replace `w-* h-*` with `size-*`; (5) update dependencies (`@radix-ui/*`, `cmdk`, etc.); (6) remove `forwardRef` using the React codemod or manually, adding `data-slot` attributes. Special considerations: deprecate `tailwindcss-animate` in favor of `tw-animate-css`, and note that HSL colors are converted to OKLCH.

Source excerpt:
> ## [Upgrade Your Project#](#upgrade-your-project)
> 
> **Important:** Before upgrading, please read the [Tailwind v4 Compatibility Docs](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/compatibility) and make sure your project is ready for the upgrade. Tailwind v4 uses bleeding-edge browser features and is designed for modern browsers.
> 
> One of the major advantages of using `shadcn/ui` is that the code you end up with is exactly what you'd write yourself. There are no hidden abstractions.
> 
> This means when a dependency has a new release, you can just follow the official upgrade paths.
> 
> Here's how to upgrade your existing projects (full docs are on the way):
> 
> ### [1\. Follow the Tailwind v4 Upgrade Guide#](#1-follow-the-tailwind-v4-upgrade-guide)
> 
> -   Upgrade to Tailwind v4 by following the official upgrade guide: [https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide)
> -   Use the `@tailwindcss/upgrade@next` codemod to remove deprecated utility classes and update tailwind config.
> 
> ### [2\. Update your CSS variables#](#2-update-your-css-variables)
> 
> The codemod will migrate your CSS variables as references under the `@theme` directive.
> 
> ```
> @layer base {
>   :root {
>     --background: 0 0% 100%;
>     --foreground: 0 0% 3.9%;
>   }
> }
>  
> @theme {
>   --color-background: hsl(var(--background));
>   --color-foreground: hsl(var(--foreground));
> }
> ```
> 
> This works. But to make it easier to work with colors and other variables, we'll need to move the `hsl` wrappers and use `@theme inline`.
> 
> Here's how you do it:
> 
> 1.  Move `:root` and `.dark` out of the `@layer` base.
> 2.  Wrap the color values in `hsl()`
> 3.  Add the `inline` option to `@theme` i.e `@theme inline`
> 4.  Remove the `hsl()` wrappers from `@theme`
> 
> ```
> :root {
>   --background: hsl(0 0% 100%); // <-- Wrap in hsl
>   --foreground: hsl(0 0% 3.9%);
> }
>  
> .dark {
>   --background: hsl(0 0% 3.9%); // <-- Wrap in hsl
>   --foreground: hsl(0 0% 98%);
> }
>  
> @theme inline {
>   --color-background: var(--background); // <-- Remove hsl
>   --color-foreground: var(--foreground);
> }
> ```
> 
> This change makes it much simpler to access your theme variables in both utility classes and outside of CSS, e.g. using color values in JavaScript.
> 
> ### [3\. Update colors for charts#](#3-update-colors-for-charts)
> 
> Now that the theme colors come with `hsl()`, you can remove the wrapper in your `chartConfig`:
> 
> ```
> const chartConfig = {
>   desktop: {
>     label: "Desktop",
> -    color: "hsl(var(--chart-1))",
> +    color: "var(--chart-1)",
>   },
>   mobile: {
>     label: "Mobile",
> -   color: "hsl(var(--chart-2))",
> +   color: "var(--chart-2)",
>   },
> } satisfies ChartConfig
> ```
> 
> ### [4\. Use new `size-*` utility#](#4-use-new-size--utility)
> 
> The new `size-*` utility (added in Tailwind v3.4), is now fully supported by `tailwind-merge`. You can replace `w-* h-*` with the new `size-*` utility:
> 
> ```
> - w-4 h-4
> + size-4
> ```
> 
> ### [5\. Update your dependencies#](#5-update-your-dependencies)
> 
> ```
> pnpm up "@radix-ui/*" cmdk lucide-react recharts tailwind-merge clsx --latest
> ```
> 
> ### [6\. Remove forwardRef#](#6-remove-forwardref)
> 
> You can use the `remove-forward-ref` codemod to migrate your `forwardRef` to props or manually update the primitives.
> 
> For the codemod, see [https://github.com/reactjs/react-codemod#remove-forward-ref](https://github.com/reactjs/react-codemod#remove-forward-ref).
> 
> If you want to do it manually, here's how to do it step by step:
> 
> 1.  Replace `React.forwardRef<...>` with `React.ComponentProps<...>`
> 2.  Remove `ref={ref}` from the component.
> 3.  Add a `data-slot` attribute. This will come in handy for styling with Tailwind.
> 4.  You can optionally convert to a named function and remove the `displayName`.
> 
> #### [Before#](#before)
> 
> ```
> const AccordionItem = React.forwardRef<
>   React.ElementRef<typeof AccordionPrimitive.Item>,
>   React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof AccordionPrimitive.Item>
> >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
>   <AccordionPrimitive.Item
>     ref={ref}
>     className={cn("border-b last:border-b-0", className)}
>     {...props}
>   />
> ))
> AccordionItem.displayName = "AccordionItem"
> ```
> 
> #### [After#](#after)
> 
> ```
> function AccordionItem({
>   className,
>   ...props
> }: React.ComponentProps<typeof AccordionPrimitive.Item>) {
>   return (
>     <AccordionPrimitive.Item
>       data-slot="accordion-item"
>       className={cn("border-b last:border-b-0", className)}
>       {...props}
>     />
>   )
> }
> ```
> 
> ## [Changelog#](#changelog)
> 
> ### [March 19, 2025 - Deprecate `tailwindcss-animate`#](#march-19-2025---deprecate-tailwindcss-animate)
> 
> We've deprecated `tailwindcss-animate` in favor of `tw-animate-css`.
> 
> New projects will have `tw-animate-css` installed by default.
> 
> For existing projects, follow the steps below to migrate.
> 
> 1.  Remove `tailwindcss-animate` from your dependencies.
> 2.  Remove the `@plugin 'tailwindcss-animate'` from your globals.css file.
> 3.  Install `tw-animate-css` as a dev dependency.
> 4.  Add the `@import "tw-animate-css"` to your globals.css file.
> 
> ```
> - @plugin 'tailwindcss-animate';
> + @import "tw-animate-css";
> ```

The `$fetch` method is typed as `Fetch<T>`, which accepts optional `InferRequestType<T>` args (containing body/query params based on the endpoint schema) and optional `ClientRequestOptions`. It returns a `Promise<ClientResponseOfEndpoint<...>>` with full response type inference. Query params are passed via the args object, body via the appropriate HTTP method property, and `ClientRequestOptions` provides additional configuration like custom fetch, headers, init overrides, and query parameter serialization.

Playwright component testing uses a "gallery" approach where components are tested via story files served by your own dev server rather than through Playwright's bundler. To set it up: 1) Create a gallery page under `playwright/gallery/` that exposes `window.mount()` and `window.unmount()`, 2) Configure `playwright.config.ts` with a project pointing `baseURL` to the gallery URL, and 3) Use `defineConfig` from `@playwright/test` (not experimental packages). The old experimental settings like `ctTemplate`, `ctCacheDir`, and `ctViteConfig` are gone — the gallery runs through your own dev server, with port configuration in `webServer` and `baseURL`. Entry files like `playwright/index.html` and `playwright/index.ts` from the experimental packages are replaced by the gallery's own `index.html` and entry module.

Per wouter@3.10.0:

The `useParams` hook returns an object containing the parameters extracted from the closest parent `<Route>` component's dynamic segments. It allows access to these parameters by name (e.g., `params.id`) or by index (e.g., `params[0]`), enabling components to access route data without prop drilling.

Source excerpt:
> This hook allows you to access the parameters exposed through [matching dynamic segments](#matching-dynamic-segments). Internally, we simply wrap your components in a context provider allowing you to access this data anywhere within the `Route` component.
> 
> This allows you to avoid "prop drilling" when dealing with deeply nested components within the route. **Note:** `useParams` will only extract parameters from the closest parent route.
> 
> ```js
> import { Route, useParams } from "wouter";
> 
> const User = () => {
>   const params = useParams();
> 
>   params.id; // "1"
> 
>   // alternatively, use the index to access the prop
>   params[0]; // "1"
> };
> 
> <Route path="/user/:id" component={User}> />
> ```

details.excerpt:
### New Features

* * *

-   Overhauled the Audio Mixer \[Warchamp7\]
    -   Adjusted the horizontal layout
    -   Adjusted the vertical layout
    -   Added button to swap layouts to the toolbar
    -   Changed the default layout to vertical
    -   Added button to toggle audio monitoring
    -   Sources in the preview are now shown while in Studio Mode
    -   Added ability to pin audio sources
        -   Pinned sources are always displayed
        -   Global audio sources are always pinned
    -   Added ability to display sources set to hide
    -   Added ability to display sources that are not in the current scene
-   Added WebRTC Simulcast Support \[Sean-Der\]
-   Added missing undo/redo actions for scene items \[cg2121\]
    -   Scale filtering, blending mode, blending method, deinterlacing mode and deinterlacing field order
-   Added partial support for Canvases to obs-websocket \[exeldro/tt2468/Warchamp7\]

### General Changes

* * *

-   Improved security of browser sources using local files \[Warchamp7\]
-   Improved plugin manager by allowing enabling/disabling missing plugins \[Warchamp7\]
-   Removed "Source" from source names \[Warchamp7\]
-   Updated the Edit Transform dialog \[Warchamp7\]
-   Changed copying a scene item to copy all properties \[cg2121/Warchamp7\]
-   Disabled dock animations \[Warchamp7\]
-   Moved transition preview button to button box \[exeldro\]
-   Rearranged default dock positions \[Warchamp7\]
-   Increased media source playback slider update rate \[Warchamp7\]
-   Enabled palette for Light theme audio mixer \[Warchamp7\]
-   Changed default bitrates to 6000 kbps \[mihawk90\]

### Bug Fixes

* * *

-   Fixed a crash if some source data was null \[Penwy\]
-   Fixed a crash on Linux when changing profiles or on application shutdown \[hoshinolina\]
-   Fixed a possible crash on macOS during application shutdown if YouTube docks were active \[PatTheMav\]
-   Fixed an issue where projector resolutions had decimals \[Warchamp7\]
-   Fixed sync of Preview/Program size and positioning \[Warchamp7\]
-   Refactored OBSBasic::Save to only save frontend canvas scenes/groups \[dsaedtler\]
-   Fixed NAL type for HEVC caption/BPM SEIs \[dsaedtler\]
-   Fixed an issue where video scaling could be incorrect in multivideo encoder scenarios \[dsaedtler\]
-   Fixed an issue with chapter markers having incorrect time when using file splitting \[garyholmes\]
-   Fixed an issue where some recordings could have black thumbnails \[derrod\]
-   Fixed an issue where the NVIDIA Blur and Background Blur could have banding or look splotchy \[pkviet\]
-   Fixed an issue where macOS Screen Capture would select an item for capture by default \[jcm93\]
-   Fixed an issue with PipeWire when capturing a device that does not require a framerate \[tytan652\]
-   Fixed an issue where PipeWire Camera framerates listed could be incorrect \[tytan652\]
-   Fixed an issue where HDR video playback in Media Source could be darker than expected \[xtfo\]
-   Fixed an issue that could cause OBS to become unable to change profiles or video settings \[exeldro\]
-   Fixed an issue that could cause transitions to become locked \[Warchamp7\]
-   Fixed audio deduplication incorrectly applying when an audio output capture source is set to monitor only \[pkviet\]

bool obs_frontend_add_dock_by_id(const char *id, const char *title, void *widget)[](#c.obs_frontend_add_dock_by_id "Link to this definition")  

Adds a dock with the widget to the UI with a toggle in the Docks menu.

When the dock is closed, a custom QEvent of type QEvent::User + QEvent::Close is sent to the widget to enable it to react to the event (e.g., unload elements to save resources). A generic QShowEvent is already sent by default when the widget is being shown (e.g., dock opened).

Note: Use [`obs_frontend_remove_dock()`](#c.obs_frontend_remove_dock "obs_frontend_remove_dock") to remove the dock

and the id from the UI.

Parameters:

-   **id** – Unique identifier of the dock
    
-   **title** – Window title of the dock
    
-   **widget** – QWidget to insert in the dock
    

Returns:

_true_ if the dock was added, _false_ if the id was already used

Added in version 30.0.
